turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doc, I came in because... I just feel like I got this motor running inside me all day long. Just revving, you know? Kinda like my buddy's old lawnmower. I was trying to help him fix it the other day, and the spark plug was totally shot. We had to walk all the way down to the hardware store on 4th street, and the guy behind the counter didn't even know what I was talking about... but anyway, what was I saying? 

Oh, right. Yeah, it's just... if I have to sit still, like at church, or out there in your clinic waiting room, or even just sitting on my own couch at home, I feel completely trapped. Like I'm gonna crawl out of my skin. I just have to get up and do something. I actually paced around the whole parking lot outside before they called my name. Did you see they're putting in new asphalt across the street? Smells like tar everywhere out there. But yeah, the sitting still thing... it's just driving me crazy.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets easily distracted by unrelated thoughts and extraneous stimuli, such as a story about a lawnmower and the smell of tar from new asphalt.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states that when expected to sit still, such as at church or in a waiting room, they 'have to get up and do something.'
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes feeling 'completely trapped' and like they are going to 'crawl out of my skin' when forced to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly states they feel like they have a 'motor running inside me all day long.'

turns.doctor_question: When you were a child, say in elementary school, did you have similar problems with sitting still and feeling restless, or is this something that's mostly started more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, man, it's been like this forever. Back when I was a boy in school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I just could not stay put. I remember Mrs. Davis in... what was it, third grade? She had this giant mole right on her chin, and every time she talked it would just wiggle. It was the craziest thing. She used to make us do these little dioramas with shoeboxes, and I made mine about dinosaurs. Used a whole bottle of that white Elmer's glue. Man, getting that glue off your hands is the best feeling, just peeling it off like snake skin... 

Wait, what was I saying? Right, school. Yeah, they'd get so mad because I talked out of turn all the time, just blurtin' stuff out. And I was always getting in trouble for jumping up out of my desk before class was even done. Soon as that big clock on the wall clicked to like, two minutes before the bell, I was already standing up. Those clocks were so loud, just clack, clack... kinda sounded like that lawnmower I was telling you about, actually.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts during the response, going on tangents about a teacher's mole and peeling glue before losing his train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient reports he could not stay put in school and would frequently jump out of his desk before class was over.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient states he talked out of turn all the time and was 'just blurtin' stuff out' in class.
